To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Shiga toxin and its B-fragment can escape from the endosomal pathway and reach the TGN by a direct transport from early/recycling to late Golgi endosomes, and that this pathway is used by cellular proteins as well.
Shiga toxin is transported from early/recycling to late endosomes, and from there to the Golgi, but bypasses the late endosomes on its way to early/recycling endosome.
Shiga toxin is taken up at 15°C and transported directly from early endosomes to the TGN in a process that is independent of the late endocytosis and that is sensitive to brefeldin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which proteins reach the Golgi complex from the endocytic and biosynthetic pathways.
the mechanisms by which Shiga toxin and related proteins are transported in mammalian cells.
the study of the intracellular transport of Shiga toxin B-subunit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
B-fragment is sorted from the early/recycling endosome and is transported to the TGN in clathrin-coated vesicles.
Shiga toxin and Shiga toxin B fragment are transported from the cell membrane to the Golgi complex via the early/recycling endosomal compartment.
the B-fragment of Shiga toxin is transported to the Golgi by a direct pathway that bypasses the late endosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Shiga toxin is transported to the Golgi via a direct pathway from early endosomes, which bypasses the late endocytotic pathway and is independent of clathrin-coated vesicles.
Shiga toxin and TGN38 share a common transport route from early/recycling to the Golgi compartments.
Shiga toxin is internalized into the cell, and then it is transported from early/recycling to the Golgi endosome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Golgi apparatus can be reached from the plasma membrane via a direct endocytic pathway.
the endosome to GolGi pathway can be studied by using Shiga toxin B fragment.
the Golgi apparatus can be directly reached by proteins that have entered cells through the plasma membrane.
